recent_decisions.decision: The leaf tufts were geometrically cubes, and the gate that could see it had to be built before the fix could be judged.
recent_decisions.why: The operator said "the bunches of leaves look a little weird, kind of like they are cubes." The first instrument grouped cards by PROXIMITY and reported 0.31 against a 0.30 threshold - nearly a false pass. Grouping exactly (one emit_sleeve call is one sleeve) showed the truth: conifer tufts were 100% parallel card pairs, broadleaf tufts 67% perpendicular plus 33% parallel. The golden-angle azimuth fix alone left 33% still near-perpendicular because the normals stayed on one circle; the tilt half is what cleared it, and stratifying those tilts in solid-angle bands (right for POINTS) measured WORSE than no tilt at all, because a sleeve is a set of PLANES. Line packing, not point scattering.

recent_decisions.decision: The canopy parity gate records the level PER SPECIES rather than widening one band.
recent_decisions.why: Broadleaf crowns land on the isotropic leaf-angle kernel almost exactly (0.94-1.05). Fir and pine sit 22% under it at every sun angle, and that is real: a fir carries flat sprays along a branch and the spherify blend pushes its normals horizontal. A single band loose enough to admit 1.30 would stop noticing a broadleaf that broke. The ratio is near-constant in sun angle for every species, so the kernel SHAPE is right and only the LEVEL is species-dependent - driving those to 1.00 wants a per-species scalar baked into the billboard atlas, which is named as the follow-up rather than hidden.

recent_decisions.decision: A three-lane merge was committed under a one-lane message and immediately reset.
recent_decisions.why: git apply --3way STAGES what it applies. recent_decisions.decision: CLOUD REPRESENTATION SURVEY (wf_2d50711f-41d) - THE DIRECTION FINDING. No shipped AAA cloud system builds cumulus BODIES out of noise. Every modern one uses noise ONLY as erosion applied to a shape that came from somewhere else. Nubis3 (SIGGRAPH 2023) is explicit: the body is an authored 8 m Dimensional Profile voxel field and the 128^3 noise is applied as ValueErosion(dimensional_profile, noise_composite) to up-rez it to 0.5 m. HumanityOS has this wiring INVERTED - inverted Worley IS our body - which is precisely the operator uniform spheres complaint. Worley cells are also near-UNIFORM in size, so the representation is structurally incapable of the POWER-LAW size distribution real cumulus fields have. SECOND FINDING, independent and immediately actionable: Nubis3 sphere-traces an SDF, step = max(sdf_distance, max(1.0, sqrt(cam_dist)*0.08)) + jitter, giving an 8 m floor at 10 km; Guerrilla measured that swap as 6.1-8.2 ms -> 2.2-4.0 ms, i.e. BETTER AND FASTER. Calibration that settles our march debate: even 2017-era 2.5D Nubis stepped 3 m near / 63 m at 16 km - our 775 m average is ~12x coarser than a nine-year-old technique. THE VERIFICATION LESSON (a checks-that-cannot-fail instance): every probe capture ever taken runs "Clear 20C 2 m/s", which is the NARROWEST possible glitter lobe (Blinn p=149, an 8 px white dot that reads as a sun). 12d ROOT CAUSE (the operator vanish-on-approach, cov100 discriminator + sentinel forensics): mesh-derived cloud rays INVERT near the ground. Proven: cov100-underdeck still blue (no legitimate gap at coverage 1.0); disabling the one-layer discard made fragments run (they rasterize as FRONT faces because the camera is outside the sagged chord plane, so front_facing==cam_inside ate everything); magenta ground-occlusion sentinel then filled the sky = downward rays. Fix: the 12d NEAR screen pass is a FULLSCREEN triangle with ANALYTIC per-pixel rays from camera-basis pads (light0/1/2 current fwd/right/up @80/96/112; light5/6/7 prev basis @160/176/192; light5.w tan(fov/2), light6.w aspect) - no mesh geometry anywhere, no facing rule needed. recent_decisions.decision: v0.1214.0 SHIPPED - THE APPROACH VANISH ROOT-CAUSED AND FIXED, plus the Ultra eyeball-rings. (1) THE VANISH (operator across ~5 rounds: most of the clouds just vanish on approach): the ATMOSPHERE DOME was painting over the composited cloud deck. The 12c order rule ran the composite BEFORE the transparent pass whenever the camera was outside the atmosphere (so the dome would veil the deck at the limb, the v0.997 look) - but over the DISC the dome alpha is near-opaque, so it ERASED the clouds. MEASURED: the composite wrote 1.2% of the disc under the old order vs 99.9% under the new one, with every discard sentinel inside the composite reading ZERO (clouds were drawn, then painted over). Fix: always composite the deck AFTER the dome - physically correct here because cloud_march_core ALREADY applies this engines aerial perspective at the first-hit distance, so the old order applied the same air column twice and the second application was opaque. Ladder proof (type+coverage pinned, one boot, screen-centre crop): before 13000km=60.9% then 9000km=8.8%, 6000=4.1%, 4000=5.6%, 2500=7.3%, 1500=8.5%, 900=9.9%; after 13000=60.8%, 9000=64.7%, 6000=61.7%, 4000=64.1%, 2500=65.1%, 1500=65.9%, 900=68.5% - the cliff is GONE and coverage is smooth 20000km->900km. (2) WHY IT MASQUERADED AS A TERRAIN BUG FOR HOURS: the cliff sat exactly at 1.5 planet radii (9556 km), the chunked-terrain proximity trigger, because chunk activation flips which shells the celestial lists carry and so flips this very ordering. Chunked-off made the cliff vanish, which sent the hunt into terrain/depth-precision territory: a distance-proportional margin on the composites depth discard was tried and REVERTED (no effect), and disabling the depth discard entirely also had no effect - both correctly falsified. The winning instrument was colour-coding EVERY discard in the composite: all read zero, which proved the fragment ran and was overdrawn rather than rejected. LESSON: when a fragment produces nothing, first prove whether it DISCARDED or was OVERDRAWN - colour every early-out; a sentinel that never fires is as informative as one that does. (3) THE ULTRA EYEBALL RINGS (operator: hypnotic pulsing rings from each spheres centre): cloud_v2_body derived its soft-rind width from the CALLERS lodb, and cloud_sun_tau calls the density function EIGHT times per shading evaluation on a geometric shadow ladder (30/57/108/206/391/743 m). Because the v2 body is a DISTANCE FIELD, the rind is a metric radius - so each sun tap shaded a concentrically SHRUNKEN copy of the same lobe and its optical-depth riser printed that copys boundary as a hard ring: six nested rings, offset sunward (the pupil), breathing as the coverage threshold drifted past. The noise body was immune because a mip level has no radius; a distance field has one. Fix: g_v2_foot_m freezes the rind ONCE per ray in cloud_march_core, so nothing downstream can vary the body scale inside one shading evaluation. Verified: Ultra lobes at 2 km are smooth domes, no bullseyes. Verify: 10-rung ladder + 8-vantage regression sweep panics=0, cloud+shader tests green, relay green, underside gates 3/4 (chroma gate has flaked warm across weather since before this change - watch item, not a regression). Open: the operators horizon line (needs a natural-weather repro; the pinned-100% attempt just puts the camera inside dense cloud, which incidentally renders near-BLACK at noon - a separate inside-cloud lighting item worth logging).

HORIZON LINE REPRODUCED (operator artifact, next item). Clean control pair captured with NATURAL weather (cloudy, no coverage pin - pinning 1.0 just buries the camera in dense cloud and proves nothing): horizon-line-6km shows the deck running to a RAZOR-SHARP cut with clear blue directly above it - no distant tops rising through the line, no haze softening it; horizon-line-under (480 m, below the deck) shows NO line at all, just a soft overcast ceiling over terrain. That matches the operator word for word ("consistent throughout the whole cloud layer until I get underneath it"). WORKING MECHANISM (to verify next round): the slab is a spherical shell with a FIXED top altitude, so the sightline grazing the slab top traces a perfect circle and the deck simply ends there. Real decks never do this because (a) cloud tops vary in height, so distant taller tops poke above the tangent, and (b) aerial perspective fades the deck out long before the geometric limit. Candidate fixes to weigh: per-column top-height variation carried into the silhouette, and/or an aerial-perspective fade that saturates before the tangent. A 3-agent analysis (fidelity-expert + code map + perf) produced hard numbers and three DISTINCT root causes, all v2-only. (1) COVERAGE WAS APPLIED TWICE. The per-cell occupancy law in 41-cloud-bodies.wgsl already sets areal coverage (p_cell = wa * cell_area / cloud_area); cloud_carve then applied the coverage THRESHOLD again, which on a distance-field body is not a coverage control at all - it is a uniform 31-77 m inward erosion of every lobe out of a 90 m rind. Consequences, measured: 40-57 percent of the 14 Pareto-distributed lobes fell below threshold and vanished (on a small cumulus ONLY the core lobe survived - one bald sphere: THE BALL PIT, with the cauliflower buds that would have hidden it being exactly what got deleted), and the 90 m density rind was crushed to a 3-18 m skin (sub-metre for isolated low-coverage clouds - a hard stencil), leaving no gradient to be translucent with so the erosion bands stippled the edge instead. Fix: CLOUD_V2_THR = 0.02 on the constructed path only (thr_base = mix(thr_noise, CLOUD_V2_THR, v2_w)), plus the domed-top/base-drop threshold shaping gated to the noise path (the SDF carries its own flat condensation base and height cap). The v0.1201 "thr -> 0 fills the slab vertically (scud)" lesson does NOT transfer: that was the noise body, where thr is the ONLY vertical shaping. (2) THE EYEBALL: crown is a pure function of `body`, and on the constructed path `body` IS distance-to-surface - so crown_shade = mix(0.62, 1.12, crown) painted a 1.81x bright arc on a contour concentric with every lobe (measured arc/interior 1.90x, predicted to 5 percent). pouch shares the defect. Both now fade out with v2_w. (3) EDGES DARKER THAN THE SKY BEHIND THEM: powder = 1 - 0.92*exp(-2*tau) returns 0.08 at a thin edge - a 12.5x darkening - and measured the rim at 0.71x the sky luminance, impossible for a conservative scatterer, and double-counted because cloud_scatter_energy already carries the dual-lobe HG phase per octave plus a two-stream diffusion floor. Floored at 0.75 on the constructed path only. Verified: rings gone, buds restored, lobes merge, clouds brighter; underside gates unchanged 3/4 (the chroma gate was already failing before this change - standing watch item); cloud + shader tests green; relay green; 5-vantage sweep panics=0. STILL OPEN and now QUANTIFIED - the TV static: the march step is 522 m minimum (slab_h * CLOUD_STEP_BAND_FRAC) rising to ~1400 m at 30 km, while the v2 density ramp is only 40 m wide (69 m after this fix). A grazing skirt ray has roughly a 38 percent chance of sampling the rind at all, so 62 percent of skirt pixels return clear sky - the grain decorrelates at 2 px, exactly one half-res accumulation texel. It is an UNCONVERGED MONTE-CARLO ESTIMATOR, not a dither. The designed cure (next increment): shade on the analytic smooth-min NORMAL, which the lobe loop can accumulate for free (n = normalize(mix(n, (p - c_i)/r_i, h_i))), replacing crown with sky-view 0.5 + 0.5*n_up and pouch with the smin blend factor as a crevice mask (seam = max 4h(1-h)) - the report costs this NET NEGATIVE - plus tying the rind or the step law together so the density ramp is actually resolved by the march.

v0.1218.0 SHIPPED - cloud SHAPE PERMANENCE, taper-merged lobes, and small clouds that stop winking out. Operator round: "the ball pit still exists... the clouds still have the TV static look... the clouds do not really seem to maintain their shape while moving around them - there is SOME shape permanence but the fine detail is weirdly non-permanent, always morphing... balls would just disappear in game never to return despite being incredibly dense looking clouds... can we taper merge the sections together... I still get the feel that the clouds are oriented to me instead of the Earth". THREE ROOT CAUSES, each matching one phrase. (1) SHAPE WAS A FUNCTION OF CAMERA DISTANCE. cloud_v2_body used rind = max(90 m, ray footprint), and the rind is the width of the density ramp - i.e. the SHAPE. The footprint is camera distance, so at the far edge of the v2 range (lodb 2 = a 4 km footprint) the rind reached 4000 m and the whole cloud dissolved into one soft gradient, then firmed into lobes as you approached. That is the morphing, and it is exactly why the clouds read as oriented to the VIEWER: their placement is planet-fixed (lat/lon cell grid) but their detail was camera-fixed. Fix: rind is now a FIXED PHYSICAL WIDTH (CLOUD_V2_RIND_M). Band-limiting is the noise mip chain and the temporal accumulation, never a reshaping of the body. (2) SMALL CLOUDS WERE BEING STEPPED OVER. The march step floor was a flat fraction of the SLAB (11.6 km x 0.045 = 522 m) while a fair-weather cumulus is 100-500 m across - so a whole cloud fitted inside ONE step and the march either sampled it or missed it entirely, and which one happened changed as the camera moved. That is a dense-looking ball winking out of existence. Fix: the floor is now SEGMENT-relative (target ~16 samples through whatever segment the ray actually crosses, clamped to the old value above and 30 m below), so long slab crossings keep their old step and their old cost while short segments - small isolated clouds and silhouette skirts, exactly where the operator sees it - get refined. First cut targeted 24 samples and cost 26 percent fps at mid-alt (24.6 -> 18.2); retuned to 16 and fps came back to 24.2 with the look held. (3) BALL PIT: the smooth-union blend floor was 1.0x the rind, so the smallest clusters read as touching spheres rather than one fused body; raised to 1.6x - this IS the operator "skirt of one model merged to another via modifiers" in SDF terms. BONUS: all four underside gates now PASS - the chroma gate had been failing for days (dark decile warmer than bright) and the finer stepping resolved the base well enough to flip it. Verified: cloud + shader tests green, relay green, 6-vantage sweep panics=0, mid-alt fps restored. STILL OPEN: a faint striation on very close large lobes (the same undersampling now showing as banding rather than noise, since the steps are smaller and more regular), and residual stipple at mid distance. The designed cure remains the fidelity report answer: shade on the analytic smooth-min NORMAL (accumulate n = normalize(mix(n, (p - c_i)/r_i, h_i)) inside the lobe loop, costed NET NEGATIVE), replacing the crown term with sky-view 0.5 + 0.5*n_up and the pouch term with the blend factor as a crevice mask.

v0.1221.0 SHIPPED - FRACTAL SURFACE DISPLACEMENT: the constructed cloud bodies stop being spheres. Operator asked two questions: "Is banding the right approach? Would gradient be better?" and "up close they are still an obvious ball pit. How do we get rid of the ball shapes?" ANSWERS: banding is not an approach, it is an artifact - discrete march steps through what should be a smooth density gradient, so gradient is exactly right and the banding is the bug. And the ball shapes cannot be blended away: no smooth-union radius can stop a union of spheres reading as spheres, because BETWEEN the blend seams the surface is still exactly spherical. Every shipped volumetric cloud system answers this the same way - noise does not BUILD the body, it DISPLACES the body surface, because a real cumulus boundary is fractal at every scale. IMPLEMENTED: two octaves of FBM displacement applied to the signed distance in METRES, at the cloud_v2_body site (post min-reduction). The perf analysis picked that site for four independent reasons, all of which matter: it is the only point where the value is still a metric distance (so the amplitude is footprint-independent - a term whose scale rides the rind is exactly the class that drew the eyeball rings); it is a pure function of world position (so the view sample and all eight sun-shadow taps see the SAME displaced surface); being post-reduction it also warps the seams BETWEEN neighbouring clouds, which is the other half of the ball-pit look, for free; and it is one fetch per sample (42 calls/ray) instead of one per lobe (882). Texture rather than procedural hash noise, specifically so the mip chain band-limits it - unfiltered value noise here would alias straight back into the salt-and-pepper it is meant to remove. The mip is taken WITHOUT the per-pixel lod dither: this displacement is SHAPE, and shape must be identical for every ray reaching a given world point or it stipples. Constants: 2.0 km / 85 m coarse (billow silhouette) + 0.55 km / 26 m fine (cauliflower rind). Verified: silhouettes are now irregular lumpy masses rather than stacked discs; fps UNCHANGED at every vantage (mid-alt 24.6, marble 17.0, under-deck 30 - the perf report had measured 4.2x headroom on the cloud pass and budgeted 1-3 taps); cloud + shader tests green; relay green; 3-vantage regression sweep panics=0; underside gates 3/4 with the chroma gate marginal at 1.130 vs 1.118 (it has flip-flopped across runs all week - genuinely flaky at ~1 percent, needs a better formulation rather than chasing). STILL OPEN: residual stipple on skirts and faint banding on very close large lobes - both the same undersampling (the march resolves a ~69 m ramp with steps floored per segment). The remaining designed cure is unchanged: shade on the analytic smooth-min NORMAL (accumulated free inside the lobe loop), replacing crown with sky-view and pouch with the blend factor as a crevice mask. NOTE for whoever picks this up: the perf report also found the near-regime frame is NOT cloud-bound - lobe-rings-ultra is 57.8 ms wall with only 12.4 ms of timed GPU and ~30 ms outside every timed stage (present/swapchain, egui, outer loop). That untimed block, not the cloud shader, is what stands between this vantage and 30 fps, and nobody owns it yet.

v0.1222.0 SHIPPED - the constructed path takes its density STRAIGHT; the eyeball rings and disc outlines are structurally gone. Operator, fourth round: "I am waiting for the ball pit look to go away... I do not know what to say or how to articulate making this look remotely real" plus a screenshot where every lobe still had a bright rim and a ringed interior. ROOT CAUSE OF THE WHACK-A-MOLE: I had been neutralising individual shading terms (crown, then pouch, then powder) while the DENSITY chain itself was still reshaping the built body. Every term in that tail is a function of `body` - dens_n (the erosion ratio, which has an interior maximum), skirt (a smoothstep over the outer 12 percent of the carve), lwp_eff (gated on the carve), and the three erosion bands feeding `base` through their (1 - base) EDGE weights. On the fractal body those are organic because `body` is a fractal; on the constructed body `body` IS distance-to-surface, so each one is a circle concentric with its lobe and they STACK into a bullseye. FIX: the constructed path now bypasses the chain entirely - its density is the displaced signed-distance ramp (dens_built = carve * lwp), mixed in by v2_w (new CloudSample.v2 field). All fractal detail now lives in the SURFACE (the two-octave FBM displacement shipped in v0.1221), which is where a real cumulus keeps it, and all remaining brightness variation must come from the sun march, i.e. from geometry. That is the principled split the analysis asked for: noise DISPLACES the surface on the built path, noise ERODES the density on the noise path. Verified at the operator scale (new vantage ultra-inside-5km, 5.5 km among the tops, plus lobe-rings-ultra): no concentric rings, no disc outlines, irregular soft masses; panics=0. PERF FINDING, and it is NOT the clouds: the operator also reported "the approach to Earth from far orbit is really bad framerate wise until I am entering atmosphere then framerate goes up". Measured frame_costs at the near-field Ultra vantage (36.91 ms = 27 fps): cpu.patch_build 6.33, gpu.celestial 6.14, cpu.chunk_veg_and_draws 3.14, gpu.cloud_screen 3.10, cpu.celestial 3.03; timed CPU 14.88 vs timed GPU 11.55, with 10.47 ms UNTIMED. The frame is CPU-BOUND and dominated by TERRAIN patch building, not by the cloud march - which is consistent with the approach being worst while chunks stream in and recovering once the working set settles inside the atmosphere. The ladder measured 23.9 fps at 30,000 km falling to 9.2 at 900 km and recovering to 18.8 at 400 km; the 900-1500 km trough is also where the 1600-2000 px crossfade runs BOTH cloud passes at once. Next perf increments, in order: (1) own the 10.47 ms untimed block (present/swapchain, egui, outer loop) - nobody does, (2) cpu.patch_build during descent, (3) narrow or cheapen the double-pass crossfade band.
